text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of stridor and wheezing worsening with neck flexion and feeding, accompanied by post-prandial vomiting, is highly suggestive of a vascular compression syndrome. To confirm this, I need to see the anatomy: REQUEST IMAGES: Neck_Ultrasound_Doppler.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. I also have Exacerbation during crying, Exacerbation during feeding, Exacerbation with neck flexion, Relief with neck extension, Occasional vomiting post-feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngeal Tracheoesophageal Diverticulum.

The combination of stridor, wheezing, and vomiting triggered specifically by feeding and neck flexion, which resolves with extension, is the classic clinical presentation of a laryngeal tracheoesophageal diverticulum. While vascular compression is a differential, the vomiting makes a diverticulum far more likely. I have requested the neck images to confirm the anatomical defect.
